title: Route 53 DNS Resolution Returns Stale IP
symptom: DNS record was updated in Route 53, but clients continue resolving the old IP address.
initial_observations: Local `dig` or `nslookup` queries still return old IP.

possible_causes.cause: High DNS TTL (Time To Live) causing public resolvers to cache old record
possible_causes.evidence_needed: Querying Route 53 authoritative nameserver returns new IP, but public 8.8.8.8 returns old IP.
possible_causes.remediation: Wait for TTL expiration or lower TTL to 60 seconds well in advance of planned migrations.

investigation_steps.title: Query Route 53 Authoritative Nameservers Directly
investigation_steps.explanation: Bypass recursive resolver caching by querying authoritative nameservers directly.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Verify authoritative server immediately returns updated IP.

verification: dig mydomain.com returns the updated IP address across public resolvers.
prevention: Lower TTL to 60-300 seconds 24-48 hours prior to DNS migrations.
